description: A coalition of non-aligned research institutions in Europe, Japan, and Canada gains momentum with an open, safety-focused AI development initiative, leveraging open-weight models to produce credible frontier-adjacent results. Their shared evaluation framework begins to attract talent and funding independently of U.S. or Chinese ecosystems, shifting perceptions of where innovation can originate.

Protests against AI data centers intensify across multiple EU member states, with local governments imposing new moratoriums on construction due to energy consumption and lack of visible public benefit. The movement gains national traction as unions in creative sectors formally align with environmental groups, framing AI infrastructure as both an economic and ecological threat.
